correctness.rationale: For all integers \(n\ge6\) and \(3\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor\), edge-stabilizer symmetry and sign antisymmetry yield \(k\) potential levels with rates \(u_i=(k-1-i)^2\) and \(d_i=i(n-2k+i)\). The Poisson system \(nI-T\) is an irreducible diagonally dominant M-matrix, while its consecutive-difference system has a positive inverse with row margin \(2(n-1)\); hence \(0<p_0<\cdots<p_{k-1}\). Detailed balance and test functions \(1\) and \(i\) give \(S_0=1/n\) and \(S_1=((k-1)+(k-1)^2/n)/(2(n-1))\). The full edge set is partitioned into sign-changing, zero-potential and adjacent-level edges; absolute summation simplifies to \(( (k+1)n^2-(k^2+3)n+2 )/(n(n-1))\). Edge transitivity makes every column equal. The projector trace gives \(R=2(1-1/\binom nk)/(k(n-k))\), so the cycle norm is \(1+\|Q\|_{1\to1}-2R\). Exact rational full-Laplacian checks passed for \((n,k)=(4,2),(5,2),(6,3),(7,3),(8,3),(8,4),(9,4)\); additional exact orbit-chain checks passed for \((n,k)=(10,5),(18,9),(40,20),(100,3),(100,50)\). The finite checks are corroboration, not a substitute for the all-integer proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary paper defines cut and cycle projections and computes Hamming-cube norms but not Johnson-graph edge-current endpoint norms. The general electrical-flow localization papers give bounds, not the exact family law. The previously established triangular Johnson graph is exactly the \(k=2\) special case, which is excluded. Published-record searches returned two Johnson vertex-projection records; their statements concern different operators and do not imply absolute sums of edge-gradient currents. The present \(k\ge3\) formulas require independent potential-sign and moment analysis. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A differently indexed electrical-network or association-scheme source may already contain the same rational law or enough stronger exact formulas to imply it.
The complete linked articles for two closely named public Johnson-scheme records could not be inspected, although their accessible summaries describe vertex-space rather than edge-space operators.
The literature search is finite and cannot certify mathematical novelty or independence.

value.rationale: The Johnson scheme is a canonical two-parameter family in discrete geometry. An exact closed-form norm for its edge cut/cycle Hodge projections gives a natural Banach-space complementability invariant and worst-case electrical-current length, rather than an arbitrary small-graph value. Nontrivial higher-rank potential ordering and moment cancellation yield a complete family law, a sharp balanced-rank maximizer, and a transition from bounded fixed-rank norms to \(n/4\) linear growth when \(k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor\). The known \(k=2\) instance is excluded from the new claim. No unstated downstream theorem is assumed.
